items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
TSD-TRS-25-009, GRT Township Transit Strategy Submission to the Ontario Transit Investment Fund
notes:
Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, introduced a presentation regarding the collaborative effort on the Township Transit Strategy. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. Adam Fraser, Principal Planner, Grand River Transit, provided further information on the funding opportunity with the Ontario Transit Investment Fund. He expanded on the plan for the Township Transit Network, public engagement conducted, and future work being phased to complete the project.

In reply to a question from the Committee, A. Fraser indicated the intent is to attempt to be able to provide greater on-demand service more broadly. Staff indicated that on-demand service can be explored based on data, which is dependent on different factors and timeframes.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner indicated stops can be explored for expansion of transit.

Replying to a question from the Committee, A. Fraser provided greater clarity on the concept of 'co-mingling.' He elaborated on the funding strategy to offset costs going forward.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
TSD-TRP-25-018, Winter Debrief Report
notes:
D. Spooner provided an introduction to the report. He indicated this report is being brought forward in response to Councillor requests as well as broader discussions on simplifying communications during snow events, and elaborated on the different types of declarations associated with declared weather and snow events. D. Spooner provided further information on challenges associated with winter maintenance and work being done to address those challenges. A video was provided which elaborated on the process for declaring events and the rationale for plowing strategies.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner agreed that a major challenge in snow events is the formation of windrows when plows come by. He indicated staff can look at the language in the policy to ensure accessibility is a priority.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner indicated that sidewalks and trails are assumed by municipal partners to be maintained throughs service agreements, but one of the points of discussion when adopting agreement going forward. He further elaborated on the work done to ensure continuity in ION service during the winter. Related to ice storms, D. Spooner answered that ice remains a significant issue for the ION, with work being done and ongoing to address these issues, including the use of alternative wires. He added that the challenge is no longer ice buildup but lighter ice that is not captured by current technology.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner provided more information on the salt quality and quantity during weather and snow events, with a significant reduction in salt use over the past two decades.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner answered where the video can be located and expanded on the public service announcement strategies to keep the public informed. He expanded on the work that is done to communicate changes that affect bus routes and transportation otherwise, focusing on the winter transit network.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner answered about the cost to clear sidewalks better in 24 hours instead of 48 hours. D. Spooner provided context to previous changes and elaborated on this service as part of area municipal agreement work. He pointed out that a challenge may be the number of times snow would be moved and would cost more, and the second challenge related to minimum maintenance standards prescribed by regulation.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to the Environment Canada system changes which indicate severity of weather.

Staff were asked to come back on exploring policies and practices in Scandinavian countries regarding sidewalk clearance.

Responding to questions, D. Spooner indicated it would be theoretically possible to look at on-demand snow clearance services, that staff can look into.

items.title: PDL-GDS-25-015, Tax Increment Grant (TIG) – Glove Box (120 Victoria Street South)
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, provided an introduction to the reports under 7.3.1 and 7.3.2, which are related and which are seeking tax increment grants for each property. He provided context for the implementation of the grant for growth and development purposes.

In reply to a question from the Committee, R. Regier provided greater clarity to the process for the grant as it applies to the various properties. He elaborated on the applicability of the program in certain areas, and the relation to municipal improvement programs.

Responding to a question from the Committee, R. Regier clarified the difference between the TIG program and the Brownfield remediation program. Amanda Kutler, TITLE, spoke to the rationale behind phasing out the Brownfield program due to costs.

items.title: Notice of Motion - Councillor Rodrigues
notes:
In reply to a question from the Committee, C. MacDonald provided more clarity on the relation of this motion to how it may impact other concerns that are being deliberated on in the budget process.

Responding to a question from the Committee, C. MacDonald clarified that residents are encouraged to reuse green bins that are no longer required for the new bin system, and there will be opportunities for residents to drop off green bins to be recycled. Olivia Kwok, Director, Waste Management, provided that the bins currently being used are encouraged to continue to be used, and added that if residents no longer want them, it would be dealt with the Circular Materials contract.

Councillor M. Harris declared an indirect pecuniary interest on this item, and refrained from discussing or voting on the matter.

motions.text: WHEREAS the implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility fully shifts responsibilities for recycling collection away from the Region of Waterloo, including decisions to reduce curbside recycling collection frequency; WHEREAS Regional staff intend to monitor changes to landfill volumes following implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility in 2026; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services and Commissioner of Resident Experience and Strategy: Engage with Circular Materials to incorporate curbside recycling collection information provided by Circular Materials in shared materials, where possible. Report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee in Q1 2027 with: Information regarding changes to the volume of waste being brought to Regional landfill following the March 2026 transition; A summary of the volume and nature of resident inquiries received by the Region regarding curbside recycling collection following the January 1, 2026 transition.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility fully shifts responsibilities for recycling collection away from the Region of Waterloo, including decisions to reduce curbside recycling collection frequency;
 
WHEREAS Regional staff intend to monitor changes to landfill volumes following implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility in 2026;
 
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services and Commissioner of Resident Experience and Strategy:

  1. Engage with Circular Materials to incorporate curbside recycling collection information provided by Circular Materials in shared materials, where possible.
  2. Report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee in Q1 2027 with:
    1. Information regarding changes to the volume of waste being brought to Regional landfill following the March 2026 transition;
    2. A summary of the volume and nature of resident inquiries received by the Region regarding curbside recycling collection following the January 1, 2026 transition.
